Heat Therapy: A warm bath or a heating pad on your abdomen can relax uterine muscles.
Gentle Exercise: Light walking or yoga can increase blood flow & reduce pain.
Pain Relievers: Over-the-counter options like ibuprofen can be effective. Consult a doctor for advice.
Hydration: Drinking plenty of water can help reduce bloating, which often makes cramps feel worse.
Iron-Rich Foods: Replenish iron lost during menstruation with foods like spinach, lentils, & red meat.
Omega-3 Fatty Acids: Found in fish & flaxseed, they have anti-inflammatory properties that can ease cramps.
Avoid Processed Foods: High sugar & salt content can worsen bloating & mood swings.
Calcium: Helps reduce muscle cramping. Found in dairy, leafy greens, & almonds.
Stay Hydrated: Dehydration is a common trigger for hormonal headaches.
Limit Caffeine & Salt: Both can contribute to dehydration & bloating.
Restful Sleep: Aim for 7-9 hours of quality sleep, as hormonal changes can disrupt sleep patterns.
Magnesium-Rich Foods: Foods like almonds, spinach, & avocados may help prevent migraines.
